title: Total beginner. Just built my own AI homelab and want to get into AI trading. Where do I start?
author: Least-Friendship4702
selftext:
Hey everyone, I'm brand new to this, so go easy on me 😅

I just finished building a dedicated AI box at home and I want to use it for automated trading, but I don't really know the right way to set it up.

My setup:

\- Ryzen 5 8500G, 16GB DDR5

\- AMD Instinct MI50 (16GB)

\- Running local Qwen models (Ollama / LM Studio)

\- Linux, on 24/7, remote access through Tailscale

\- Accounts on Robinhood and Coinbase

What I have so far: a basic Python bot running in paper mode (fake money). It's a simple trend strategy (EMA crossover + RSI with stop-losses), and my local LLM reviews each trade before it goes through. Backtests show the fast/hourly version just bleeds money to fees, and the slow daily version barely makes anything, so I know I'm missing a lot.

My questions:

1. What's the right role for a local LLM in trading? Should it make the trade decisions, filter trades, read news/sentiment, or something else?

2. Is Robinhood/Coinbase fine for bots, or should I switch to something like Alpaca or IBKR?

3. How long did you paper trade before going live, and how much did you start with?

4. Any good resources (books, YouTube, GitHub repos) for learning backtesting the right way and not fooling myself?

5. Biggest beginner mistakes you'd tell me to avoid?

I'm not expecting to get rich. I just want to learn this the right way and not blow up my account. Any advice is appreciated 🙏
